title: Decomposers and Matter Cycling Review Test
description: Trace matter through dead material, decomposers, air, soil, and plants using evidence and system boundaries.

questions.prompt: A fallen apple loses visible tissue. Where could its carbon be a month later?
questions.questionText: A fallen apple loses visible tissue. Where could its carbon be a month later?
options: In decomposer biomass and carbon dioxide as well as remaining tissue.
Only in the original apple shape.
Only in mineral nitrogen.
In heat with no remaining carbon atoms.
questions.correctAnswer: In decomposer biomass and carbon dioxide as well as remaining tissue.
questions.explanation: Carbon can move among several material pools without becoming heat or nitrogen.

questions.prompt: An aquarium model shows fish waste -> microbes. Which added route shows matter returning to producers?
questions.questionText: An aquarium model shows fish waste -> microbes. Which added route shows matter returning to producers?
options: Microbial breakdown -> dissolved mineral nutrients -> algae.
Microbial heat -> algae as carbon atoms.
Microbes -> destroyed waste atoms -> algae.
Waste -> sunlight -> algae.
questions.correctAnswer: Microbial breakdown -> dissolved mineral nutrients -> algae.
questions.explanation: Mineral nutrients can return to producers; energy and atoms must be distinguished.

questions.prompt: A dry sample shrinks from 24 g to 18 g. A matched second sample shrinks from 24 g to 21 g. Which statement compares the losses?
questions.questionText: A dry sample shrinks from 24 g to 18 g. A matched second sample shrinks from 24 g to 21 g. Which statement compares the losses?
options: The first lost three times as much dry mass.
The second lost more dry mass.
Both lost one quarter of their initial mass.
The first lost twice as much dry mass.
questions.correctAnswer: The first lost twice as much dry mass.
questions.explanation: Losses are 6 g and 3 g, so the first loss is twice the second.

questions.prompt: A leaf's wet mass increases after rain although its tissue is breaking down. What would improve the comparison?
questions.questionText: A leaf's wet mass increases after rain although its tissue is breaking down. What would improve the comparison?
options: Conclude decomposition reversed.
Use comparable dry-mass measurements to separate water from tissue change.
Use rainwater mass as new leaf tissue.
Measure only surface color.
questions.correctAnswer: Use comparable dry-mass measurements to separate water from tissue change.
questions.explanation: Water uptake can hide organic-material loss in wet-mass measurements.

questions.prompt: Why might nutrient cycling slow in a very dry habitat?
questions.questionText: Why might nutrient cycling slow in a very dry habitat?
options: Low moisture can reduce decomposer activity and nutrient release.
Dryness removes all mineral elements from existence.
Decomposers obtain their food only from rain.
Dead matter changes directly into sunlight.
questions.correctAnswer: Low moisture can reduce decomposer activity and nutrient release.
questions.explanation: Moisture can limit biological activity; atoms still exist.

questions.prompt: A garden model says plants get all their body carbon from compost through roots. What revision is needed?
questions.questionText: A garden model says plants get all their body carbon from compost through roots. What revision is needed?
options: Show heat entering roots as carbon.
Show carbon dioxide entering leaves for photosynthesis and minerals entering roots.
Remove compost because minerals never matter.
Show water entering roots as the main source of carbon.
questions.correctAnswer: Show carbon dioxide entering leaves for photosynthesis and minerals entering roots.
questions.explanation: Plant carbon and mineral nutrients enter by different routes.

questions.prompt: Dry leaves vanish from an exposed plot but gather against a nearby fence. Which process is directly supported?
questions.questionText: Dry leaves vanish from an exposed plot but gather against a nearby fence. Which process is directly supported?
options: All missing leaves were respired.
Wind transported leaf matter out of the plot.
The plot's atoms were converted to light.
The fence increased photosynthesis in dead leaves.
questions.correctAnswer: Wind transported leaf matter out of the plot.
questions.explanation: The relocated leaves provide direct evidence of transport across the boundary.

questions.prompt: A theoretical system has 80 tracked carbon units. Remaining litter has 30 and gas has 35; organisms hold the rest. What is the organism pool?
questions.questionText: A theoretical system has 80 tracked carbon units. Remaining litter has 30 and gas has 35; organisms hold the rest. What is the organism pool?
options: 15 units.
45 units.
50 units.
65 units.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would challenge a claim that colder conditions caused slower leaf breakdown?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would challenge a claim that colder conditions caused slower leaf breakdown?
options: Cold samples were repeated three times.
All samples used the same leaf type.
The colder samples also had much less moisture.
All results were measured after the same time.
questions.correctAnswer: The colder samples also had much less moisture.
questions.explanation: Different moisture offers a competing cause; repetition alone does not remove that confound.

questions.prompt: A decomposer releases heat while using a dead leaf. Why is this consistent with energy conservation?
questions.questionText: A decomposer releases heat while using a dead leaf. Why is this consistent with energy conservation?
options: Energy has stopped existing.
Carbon atoms have become temperature.
The decomposer has created energy from nothing.
Energy has transferred to the surroundings and is less available to the food web.
questions.correctAnswer: Energy has transferred to the surroundings and is less available to the food web.
questions.explanation: Heat leaving an organism is energy transfer, not energy destruction.

questions.prompt: A model has soil minerals -> roots -> leaf -> dead litter. Which link completes this nutrient cycle?
questions.questionText: A model has soil minerals -> roots -> leaf -> dead litter. Which link completes this nutrient cycle?
options: Dead litter -> sunlight -> soil minerals.
Dead litter -> heat -> roots.
Dead litter -> disappearing atoms -> minerals.
Dead litter -> decomposer activity -> soil minerals.
questions.correctAnswer: Dead litter -> decomposer activity -> soil minerals.
questions.explanation: Decomposition helps return nutrients to the nonliving environment.

questions.prompt: A soil-only comparison releases 4 units of gas and matched soil-plus-leaf samples release 9. What is the measured increase associated with added leaves?
questions.questionText: A soil-only comparison releases 4 units of gas and matched soil-plus-leaf samples release 9. What is the measured increase associated with added leaves?
options: 9 units because soil respiration does not count.
13 units because the comparison must be added.
5 units, with replication needed to check consistency.
4 units because only the comparison is evidence.
questions.correctAnswer: 5 units, with replication needed to check consistency.
questions.explanation: The difference is 9 - 4 = 5, and replication helps assess reliability.

questions.prompt: A forest loses decomposers but still receives sunlight. Why might plant growth eventually slow?
questions.questionText: A forest loses decomposers but still receives sunlight. Why might plant growth eventually slow?
options: Sunlight can no longer contain carbon.
Plants must eat decomposers directly to photosynthesize.
Mineral recycling can decline even while light remains available.
All carbon dioxide disappears immediately.
questions.correctAnswer: Mineral recycling can decline even while light remains available.
questions.explanation: Light alone does not supply every needed material; nutrients can become limiting.

questions.prompt: A decay study measures leaves, gas, and microbes, but water drains away unmeasured. What limitation remains?
questions.questionText: A decay study measures leaves, gas, and microbes, but water drains away unmeasured. What limitation remains?
options: The measured pools necessarily contain every atom.
Dissolved or suspended matter may leave in the drainage.
Water cannot transport any leaf-derived matter.
Drainage changes only energy, never matter.
questions.correctAnswer: Dissolved or suspended matter may leave in the drainage.
questions.explanation: A system accounting must include material crossing every relevant boundary.

questions.prompt: A student argues that matter cycling means no new energy is needed. Which reply uses both ecosystem models?
questions.questionText: A student argues that matter cycling means no new energy is needed. Which reply uses both ecosystem models?
options: Reused atoms create unlimited usable energy.
Decomposers turn all dispersed heat back into sunlight.
Atoms can be reused while energy disperses, so continued energy input is needed.
Recycling minerals stops respiration from using energy.
questions.correctAnswer: Atoms can be reused while energy disperses, so continued energy input is needed.
questions.explanation: Matter cycling and energy flow are distinct; recycling atoms does not recover all dispersed energy.
